en: The Apadāna of the Elder Vallikāraphaladāyaka From the Naḷamāli Chapter, Number Eight I gave a vallikāra fruit to the Buddha, the Great Sage, the Teacher who has reached the further shore. Because of that root of merit, I have been reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. Having passed through the cycle of existence, I have now attained final liberation. I am a disciple of the Buddha, one who has reached the end of suffering. This is my true nature; this is my lineage. This is my own personal history. I have paid homage to the feet of the Blessed One. May there be well-being. May there be well-being. May there be well-being. May there be well-being. May there be well-being. “At that time, the Perfectly Enlightened One named Sumana was dwelling in Takkarā;
having taken a vallikāra fruit, [he gave it to me].”
I gave [it] to the Self-Existent One.
that was the fruit of the gift I then gave.
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of giving fruit.
The defilements have been burnt away by me.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Vallikāraphaladāyaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Vallikāraphaladāyaka is the eighth.
